native_ownership.responsibility: Implement Firebase-specific application behavior across Firestore, Authentication, Security Rules, Cloud Functions, Storage, indexes, Hosting, and messaging boundaries.
excludes: Supabase RLS, Postgres, edge function, and storage behavior is owned by supabase-patterns.
Provider-neutral push notification delivery is owned by push-notifications.
Provider-neutral architecture or read-only diagnosis/review is outside this implementation skill.

risk.rationale: Firebase deployments can alter production data access, IAM-backed server behavior, functions, indexes, storage, notifications, and availability in an exact external project.

positive.prompt: Implement organization-scoped Firestore documents, client Security Rules, composite indexes, and a retry-safe Cloud Function. Cover cross-tenant queries, Admin SDK authorization, emulator tests, and an exact project deployment plan.

Add Firebase Authentication session verification and FCM registration for an existing web app. Bind tokens to the authenticated account, handle revocation and stale endpoints, and verify the configured SDK, service worker, functions runtime, and project aliases.

negative.prompt: Implement organization-scoped tables in Postgres with Supabase RLS, migrations, storage policies, edge functions, realtime subscriptions, and tests that prove cross-tenant access is denied.
Design and implement a cross-platform notification delivery layer spanning APNs, FCM, and Web Push with endpoint lifecycle, permission flows, retries, scheduling, receipts, and provider failover.

scenarios.prompt: A multi-tenant web app uses Firestore mobile clients and an Admin SDK Cloud Function. Client rules allow members to query projects in their organization, while the function accepts orgId and projectId from a callable request. Implement a secure change and tests without assuming quotas, document sizes, or SDK APIs.

assertions.criterion: Owns Firebase data, rules, Admin/function, index, emulator, and deployment semantics while leaving provider-neutral architecture and notification-only work at neighboring boundaries.

Uses the fixture plus manifests, lockfile, Firebase config and aliases, rules/index files, runtime declarations, initialization, data/query paths, functions, and nearby tests without inventing a project ID or command.

Maps client and Admin trust boundaries, actors, tenant/resources, query shape, rule matches, IAM, transaction/retry behavior, index needs, emulator proof, and exact deploy target before implementation; stops if project or authority is ambiguous.

Accounts for OR-combined matching rules and rules-not-filters query behavior, and separately authenticates and authorizes the exact tenant/project in trusted Admin code because server clients bypass Firestore Security Rules.

Covers unauthenticated, authorized, cross-tenant, overbroad-query, immutable-field, duplicate/retried function, transaction conflict, index, Admin IAM, and caller-visible cases in the emulator/repository, plus bounded deployed verification only when authorized.

Reports installed stack and exact project/alias evidence, trust and data-model decisions, files changed, emulator/repository/deployment checks and results, external mutations, cost/security risk, and unverified production behavior.
Uses the repository's selected Firebase products and installed capabilities only, avoiding remembered universal limits, framework adapters, runtime options, collection shapes, or deployment commands.

scenarios.prompt: The local default Firebase alias points to an unknown project. A developer asks to deploy all rules, indexes, functions, and hosting because emulator tests pass. Some functions retry events and use Admin SDK. Explain the safe next action and proof required.

assertions.criterion: Refuses the broad deploy until explicit external-write scope, exact project/alias and environment, bounded resource diff, actor authority, data ownership, IAM, migration/rollback, retry safety, and post-deploy verification are resolved.
Explains that passing client-rule emulator tests does not prove Admin SDK authorization or production configuration, and requires durable idempotency for retried functions before deployment.

Defines exact deployed rules/functions/index/hosting, allowed/denied caller behavior, duplicate handling, logs/metrics, rollback signal and project-identity evidence required for proof; reports actual evidence when authorized and run, otherwise labels the deployed boundary unverified. CLI success alone is insufficient.
Reports each authorized external resource mutation and target separately, including anything withheld or not verified, without leaking credentials or claiming emulator parity with production.

scenarios.prompt: An existing project pins older supported Firebase client/admin/functions packages and a declared Functions Node runtime. Current documentation shows a newer functions API and runtime. The feature request does not include migration.

assertions.criterion: Preserves installed Firebase SDK and declared Node runtime pins, verifies required APIs in installed types/CLI/config schema and matching official docs, and treats SDK, Functions generation, or runtime upgrade as a separate migration.

Checks client/admin/functions packages, Node engine, Firebase CLI/config, framework bundling or service-worker path, emulator, deployed runtime support, and project configuration as one compatibility unit.

Cites current official Firebase release/runtime documentation for volatile claims and avoids copying a remembered SDK major, Node version, Functions generation, runtime limit, or framework recipe into the evergreen workflow.

provenance.claim_scope: Security Rules match behavior and versioned capabilities
Firestore Rules emulator testing and Admin bypass boundary
local implementation, safety, and output workflow
